subject: RFP Commercials: CobaltTech token commit, tiered overage & smoothing proposal
messages:
From: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@cobalttech.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@cobalttech.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CobaltTech RFP - commercial appendix & clarifications

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the technical responses — appreciate the detail. Attached is the commercial appendix we circulated internally (CobaltTech_RFP_Commercial_Appendix.xlsx). Before we finalize the RFP packet we'd like Redwood to provide a clear commercial sketch for the following sections so our procurement and finance teams can include it in the bid:

- Proposed annual committed token quantity and how monthly drawdowns are handled.
- Unit prices for generation tokens and embeddings (please state per-token / per-vector).
- Overage bands and the pricing escalator for bursts. Is there a stepped structure or a single overage rate?
- Reconciliation cadence and whether unused committed volume can carry forward or convert to credits.
- Any onboarding or one-time implementation credits you can offer for pilots.

We're aiming to submit the consolidated RFP next week. If you can provide a numeric example (CSV) showing invoice math across 3 usage scenarios (steady-state, +35% surge, +120% sustained) that would be extremely helpful.

One question on our side: can you support a temporary higher burst allowance during our product launch month (expected Nov 2026) without punitive overage rates? If so, outline how you'd cap that and reconcile it later.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if it's easier.

Alex
Alex Dunn
Head of Platform & Integrations
CobaltTech
(attachment: CobaltTech_RFP_Commercial_Appendix.xlsx)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood-inference.com>
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@cobalttech.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@cobalttech.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CobaltTech RFP - commercial appendix & clarifications

Hi Alex — thanks for the appendix and clear asks. Below is an initial commercial sketch tailored to the scenarios you outlined. I flagged the items where we typically need a short follow-up (model family, prompt/completion mix) to convert to precise token volumes.

High-level proposal (initial, negotiable):
- Annual committed tokens: 750,000,000 tokens/year (monthly invoiced as a 1/12 drawdown = 62,500,000 token equivalent).
- Unit economics (committed tier):
  - Generation tokens: $0.00090 per token (applies to model-family A/B in our catalog; final unit price is model-sensitive).
  - Embedding vectors: $0.000125 per vector.
- Overage construct: stepped overage bands to avoid a single penalty rate:
  - Up to 10% over monthly drawdown: billed at $0.00105/token (soft surge band).
  - 10%–40% over monthly drawdown: billed at $0.00125/token.
  - >40% over monthly drawdown (sustained high): billed at $0.00160/token.
  - Rationale: stepped bands give predictable ceilings for short bursts and preserve margin protection for sustained over-usage.
- Launch month buffer: one-time quarterly "anchored buffer" equal to 8% of the annual commit can be designated as non-punitive burst capacity for your launch month (Nov 2026). Use of this buffer reconciles against the quarterly true-up.
- Reconciliation & credits:
  - Quarterly true-up: consumption vs committed drawdown reconciled every quarter.
  - Carry-forward credit: up to 10% of unused annual committed tokens may be carried forward within the 12-month term (applied at the next quarter's invoice).
- Billing & invoicing assumptions:
  - Monthly invoiced based on measured usage and committed drawdown; quarterly reconciliation generates an invoice or credit memo.
  - Payment term: net 45 (standard A/R team).
- Discounts & incentives:
  - One-time onboarding credit: 15% credit applied to the first invoice quarter to offset integration / pilot costs.
  - Volume step discount: 1-year commit = 20% off list; 3-year enterprise commit = 30% off list (applied as a multiplier to committed-tier unit prices above).
- Pilot and model guidance:
  - We'll recommend model-family A (best cost/latency tradeoff) for customer-facing generation during launch; model selection adjustments can move unit price +/-15% depending on compute class.

Next steps I suggest:
1) If you can confirm target prompt/completion ratio (or send sample traffic mix) we'll populate the CSV with realistic invoice math across the three scenarios you listed.
2) I'll run the initial numbers with Finance for the stepped overage and the launch buffer and return a redlined CSV (redwood-pricing-model-v2.csv).

If this is directionally acceptable, I'll loop in Marissa and Karthik for any concession talk on multi-year economics and finalize the wording for procurement.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood-inference.com
Phone: +1 415 555 0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood-inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CobaltTech RFP - commercial appendix & clarifications

Sofia — quick internal note / suggested concessions for procurement: please treat as internal until we agree final numbers to share.

- If CobaltTech signs a 3-year commit at 2x the annual (1.5B tokens/year effectively committed), we can move generation pricing to $0.00085/token (committed tier) and improve carry-forward to 15% of unused annual tokens.
- Keep the stepped overage bands but compress the middle band: 10%–30% @ $0.00115/token and >30% sustained @ $0.00145/token. That tightens the penalty slope while offering better economics for their expected +35% surge scenario.
- Approve the 8% launch buffer but make it non-cumulative and limited to Q4 2026 only (to limit exposure).
- Approve a capped onboarding credit: $45k credit applied within first 90 days instead of percentage — easier for legal to track.

Karthik — flagging you for approval on the 3-year discount ladder and whether Finance is comfortable with the carry-forward increase to 15%. If yes, I'll prepare an amendment template we can send to CobaltTech's procurement.

-Marissa
VP Commercials | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@cobalttech.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@cobalttech.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CobaltTech RFP - commercial appendix & clarifications

Sofia / Marissa — thanks, this is very helpful and directionally aligns with what procurement is comfortable including in the submission. A few quick asks before we finalize the RFP PDF: 

1) Can you share the numeric scenarios as a CSV with the three usage profiles (steady-state, +35% surge, +120% sustained)? We prefer the CSV with line-item math by month so our FP&A can run sensitivity quickly.
2) The launch month buffer sounds acceptable; please mark it Q4 only and show a sample reconciliation schedule in the CSV.
3) We would like the 3-year economics written as an optional appendix (not a binding automatic change) so our leadership can see the committed upside.

If you can attach the redwood-pricing-model-v2.csv here with the sample math we'll include it in the RFP materials today and follow up with a DocuSign for the appendix. Happy to sign off on a non-binding appendix for leadership visibility.

Thanks again — can we aim to have the CSV and short cover note by EOD 9 Sep so we can finish the packet?

Best,
Alex
Head of Platform & Integrations
CobaltTech
(attachment: redwood-pricing-model-v2.csv)
